inventory.name: plane-detection feature descriptor in an immersive-ar session request
XRPlane: planeSpace, polygon, orientation, semanticLabel, lastChangedTime

syntax.rationale: The executable requestSession('immersive-ar', { requiredFeatures: ['plane-detection'] }) call is the actual session-options dictionary form, rather than an inline name presented as grammar.

errors.rationale: The example guards against a missing plane pose; it does not describe how a session request fails when required plane detection is unsupported. The page does not provide complete failure handling for this descriptor.

compatibility.rationale: The page provides a browser table, but its Chrome 147 ship/default claim conflicts with the fetched ChromeStatus feature record; see notes.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The page describes the physical-environment geometry exposed to apps, but does not cover the draft's §6 privacy mitigations (quantizing poses or polygons, or withholding planes). This documents the exposure surface, not the mitigations; see notes.

syntax.rationale: The render-loop code reads frame.detectedPlanes and iterates the resulting collection, using the real XRFrame property access form.

errors.rationale: The example guards absent getPose results but does not mention the spec's InvalidStateError if detectedPlanes is read on an inactive XRFrame. This property-specific error is omitted from the page.

lifecycle.rationale: The example reads detectedPlanes once per animation frame; it does not spell out the draft's initial empty set or update algorithm.

compatibility.rationale: The table reports Chrome 147 default support; the fetched ChromeStatus record instead reports Android 77 origin trial and no desktop milestone; see notes.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The page lists the plane geometry made available by the collection; it does not explain the draft's §6 option to omit planes from the set for privacy. This is an omission, not a claim that the mitigation is covered.

syntax.rationale: The runnable example accesses plane.planeSpace, plane.orientation, plane.semanticLabel, and plane.polygon; the XRPlane object table also names lastChangedTime. These are readonly interface properties, not constructor options.

inputs.rationale: The plane attributes are returned by the AR tracking system, not supplied as an XRPlane constructor input; the table identifies the platform-derived geometry and classifications.

errors.rationale: The example explicitly checks for null from frame.getPose(plane.planeSpace, referenceSpace); it does not describe any other failure modes or stale tracking behavior for XRPlane.

lifecycle.rationale: The table's lastChangedTime records plane-data updates, while the render-loop example repeatedly reads planes; the draft clarifies that pose changes do not update this timestamp, which the page does not state.

compatibility.rationale: The page supplies a browser table for this module, though its Chrome support statements disagree with the fetched ChromeStatus record; see notes.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The table lists exposed real-world coordinates, boundary and semantic label. It does not document draft §6 mitigation of physical-environment detail by rounding polygons, quantizing poses or dropping planes; see notes.

notes: On 2026-10-06 the page states that plane detection shipped by default in Chrome 147 desktop and Android; the linked ChromeStatus feature 5732397976911872, fetched 2026-10-06 (its rendered URL is a JS shell; its API record was also fetched at https://chromestatus.com/api/v0/features/5732397976911872), instead reports Origin trial, Android milestone 77 and desktop null; neither claim is adjudicated here. On 2026-10-06 the page describes exposed physical-environment plane geometry without privacy mitigations, while the linked WebXR Plane Detection Module Editor's Draft §6, fetched 2026-10-06 at https://immersive-web.github.io/plane-detection/, says user agents may reduce polygon detail, quantize plane poses or withhold planes entirely to limit physical-environment exposure; neither account is adjudicated here, and this is a page omission. The draft also specifies InvalidStateError on inactive-frame detectedPlanes access and defines XRSession.initiateRoomCapture(), neither covered by this page's render-loop example; the inventory intentionally follows this page's documented surface, not the full moving draft. No page prose was changed.
